_comment: Building catalog for the settlement build menu. category: 'resource' (ticks a resource), 'housing' (hard-gates recruitment of a species until built), 'functional' (unlocks an action button), or 'main' (the player's home -- auto-placed at game start, not buildable, not removable, has hp and is the Crusade's target). 'requires' is another building_id that must already exist in the settlement before this one appears in the build menu (empty string = always available). Costs: Bone Pile/Dark Altar cost the resource they themselves refine (Bones/Dark Essence); everything else is ordinary construction and costs Wood/Stone, the resources Workers gather (see WorkerSystem.gd) -- Dark Essence stays a separate ritual/magic resource, not a construction material.
_comment_barracks: The Barracks is category 'housing_intake' -- a category of exactly one, and deliberately not 'housing' (that category means the old per-species hard gate, now locked). It is the recruit intake building per FOUNDATION_SPEC section 9: 'capacity' residents, 'unique': true so only one can ever exist (BuildingCatalog.buildable_ids drops it from the menu once placed), and no 'requires' -- GAME_OUTLINE Stage 2 puts the Barracks *first*, before the Workshop tech line, so gating it behind the Workshop would invert the intended build order. Its Upgrade button exists in the Barracks panel but is hard-locked, per the same section.
_comment_locked: 'locked': true keeps an entry in the catalog but out of the build menu -- BuildingCatalog.buildable_ids() filters it. Used by the Stage-1-3 foundation reset (see CLAUDE.md) for the Dark Altar (its Dark Essence loop is Stage 4) and the five old per-species housing buildings (superseded by the Barracks-intake + fund-a-house model in FOUNDATION_SPEC section 9 and the housing_style rules in RACES.md). They are deliberately NOT deleted: EventSystem's housing gate and ThreatSystem still reference the same data shape, and these entries are the reference for whatever replaces them.
